items.title: Securities class action (Patel v. Edwards Lifesciences) alleging misleading statements on TAVR demand and inadequate internal controls between February and July 2024, following a 31% fall in the stock on 25/07/2024.
items.allegedBy: Investisseurs actionnaires (plusieurs cabinets dont Robbins Geller, BFA Law, Levi & Korsinsky) - class action devant le U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, No. 24-cv-02221
items.outcome: Motion to dismiss partially granted/denied on 19/09/2025; agreement in principle for an amount not material to the financial statements (charge booked in Certain Litigation Expenses), subject to court approval

items.title: Shareholder derivative action (Ho v. Zovighian) alleging violations of federal securities laws, breaches of fiduciary duty, abuse of control and mismanagement, in connection with the same facts as the Patel action.
items.allegedBy: Shareholder (Manh Ho), on behalf of the company, against certain officers and directors - U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, Case No. 8:24-cv-02822

items.title: FTC preliminary injunction blocking the planned acquisition of JenaValve Technology (945 M$) on anticompetitive grounds in the nascent TAVR-AR (aortic regurgitation) segment.
items.outcome: Preliminary injunction granted in January 2026; Edwards abandoned the acquisition and terminated the merger agreement on 14/01/2026 rather than pursue the litigation
items.source: Legal press coverage (MedTech Dive, Arnold & Porter) - already documented in detail in hypothese.text

items.title: FTC/DOJ settlement for violation of the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act: structuring of the JC Medical acquisition (2024) to avoid the prior antitrust notification, directly linked to the aborted attempt to acquire JenaValve.
items.allegedBy: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) et Department of Justice (DOJ)
items.outcome: Civil penalty of 10 M$ for Edwards (2 M$ for Genesis MedTech/JC Medical) - the largest combined settlement ever obtained by the agencies for this type of failure; strengthened prior-notification obligation and an antitrust compliance programme to be put in place
items.source: FTC (communiqué du 13/07/2026), Arnold & Porter, MedTech Dive, Bloomberg Law

clesRetenues: Q Robbie Marcus (JPMorgan) - drivers of TAVR growth (market vs share) and TMTT mix: growth driven by SAPIEN technology/clinical evidence, similar US and international growth, broad TMTT strength across PASCAL/EVOQUE/M3.
Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo) - why split the PROGRESS presentation (baseline characteristics vs results): pedagogical choice on moderate stenosis, 2026 impact judged minimal.

Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo, follow-up) - is 10% group growth achievable in 2027 given the implied H2 slowdown: long-term 10% target reaffirmed, detailed 2027 guidance promised at the investor conference.
Q Travis Steed (BofA) - normalised seasonality in Q3 and expected pace of TAVR growth: normal sequential increase expected, exceptional Q2 25 comparisons explaining the apparent H2 slowdown.

Q Travis Steed (BofA, follow-up) - impact of the NCD on TAVR centre expansion and TMTT capacity: draft policy favourable to asymptomatic coverage, no major centre expansion expected, efficiency gains in prospect.

Q Joanne Wuensch (Citi) - adoption timeline and revenue contribution if PROGRESS is a success: treating moderate stenosis will require a change in practice and medical education, clarity expected at TCT.

Q Pito Chickering (Deutsche Bank) - PASCAL tricuspid approval timeline (Q4) and competitive positioning: FDA approval expected in Q4 after the data presentation at TCT, European experience demonstrating PASCAL differentiation.
Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore ISI) - EVOQUE-specific inflection or broad TMTT growth: broad growth across all TMTT platforms, EVOQUE with strong momentum through the opening of new centres.
Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore ISI, follow-up) - PROGRESS baseline characteristics (heart failure, treatments): PROGRESS is not a heart failure trial, patients with healthy left ventricular function.

Q Josh Jennings (TD Cowen) - TAVR-in-TAVR opportunity and timing of volume contribution: market share currently low but growth expected, already embedded in the market models with durability considerations.
Q David Roman (Goldman Sachs) - reading of competing TAVR durability data and impact on device choice: clinical evidence reinforces confidence in SAPIEN durability and physician demand.
Q David Roman (Goldman Sachs, follow-up) - drivers of the strong sequential TMTT growth and share dynamics: PASCAL/EVOQUE/SAPIEN M3 portfolio differentiation enabling personalised therapy selection.

Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo) - market share assumptions in the TAVR guidance given competing durability data: majority of the growth reflects market expansion, modest share gains driven mainly by a competitor exit in Europe.

Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo, follow-up) - timeline of the confirmatory clinical work on SAPIEN X4: evidence collection planned through 2026, product improvements to be communicated after the trial ends.
Q Travis Steed (BofA) - structural heart lab capacity constraints on volumes: capacity not critical, health systems managing effectively through process optimisation.

Q Travis Steed (BofA, follow-up) - assessment of the proposed NCD requirements and pace of US TAVR growth: final NCD decision hard to predict, provisional decision expected in June, healthy US growth, ex-US faster.
Q Robbie Marcus (JPMorgan) - why the TAVR guidance was raised by only 1% despite solid beats: prudent approach reflecting a low Q1 25 comparison and an already high Q2 25 base.
Q Robbie Marcus (JPMorgan, follow-up) - are competitors losing share to Edwards in mitral/tricuspid: Edwards is creating category expansion rather than simply taking share.

Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore ISI) - impact of the accelerated buyback programme on the share count: the ASR reduces the average diluted share count by 5 million over the year, nominal weather impact in Q1.

Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore ISI, follow-up) - confidence level on the PROGRESS trial and management of crossovers: no comment on trials before results, presentation at TCT, rapid enrolment reflecting physician enthusiasm.
Q Joanne Wuensch (Citi) - modelling of upcoming R&D and progress of the CFO search: R&D guidance maintained at 17%, CFO search well advanced, announcement to come.
Q Matthew Taylor (Jefferies) - does the TAVR guidance raise reflect share gains or mainly market growth: Q1 outperformance driven mainly by market growth, modest share gains.

Q Matthew Taylor (Jefferies, follow-up) - impact of the macro environment on coverage and procedure demand: no strained environment observed, robust demand for life-saving technologies, new FDA-CMS RAPID policy judged positive.
Q Matt Miksic (Barclays) - launch strategy for the SAPIEN M3 mitral replacement: early-phase rollout starting with the trial centres, gradual extension.

pointsCles: Broad-based beat: sales of $1.74B grew 12.5% underlying with all franchises contributing (TAVR $1.30B +10.5%, TMTT $195.9M +44.8%, Surgical $284M +5%); adjusted EPS $0.78 beat by $0.04 while GAAP EPS was $0.42 due to the California R&D tax credit limitation.

FY26 guidance raised on sales (total 10-11%, TAVR 8-9%, TMTT $760-780M) but adjusted EPS only reaffirmed at $2.95-3.05: operating leverage (op margin at high end of 28-29%, ~150bps constant-currency expansion) absorbs a tax rate now expected at the high end of 16-19% (Pillar Two without safe harbor legislation plus California R&D credit limits).

Regulatory and clinical catalysts stacked in H2: final CMS TAVR NCD expected in September (draft seen as favorable on asymptomatic coverage pathway and heart-team modernization), full PROGRESS moderate-AS results at TCT, CLASP IITR data plus US PASCAL tricuspid launch and next-gen PASCAL Capture Clarity approvals expected in Q4.

Management flagged that H2 underlying growth will look artificially low against unusually strong summer-2025 comps (Q3 guide: sales $1.63-1.71B, adjusted EPS $0.71-0.77) and reiterated long-term targets of ~10% average sales growth, 50-100bps annual operating margin expansion and TMTT reaching $2B revenue by 2030.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Edwards Lifesciences is the global TAVR leader, riding a clinical-practice shift (early treatment of severe aortic stenosis) that drove another guidance raise at Q2 (group +10-11% cc, TAVR +8-9%). TMTT keeps scaling (+45% cc in Q2; EVOQUE/PASCAL/SAPIEN M3) toward its 2bn$-by-2030 target. The core thesis - ~10%/yr revenue growth 2026-2030 with 50-100bp/yr adjusted operating-margin expansion from 2027 - is intact and reinforced. What changed this year is financial, not operational: (i) a durably higher normative tax (Pillar Two + California R&D credit limitation; management explicitly guiding the top of 16-19%) and (ii) net cash rebased down (2.3bn$ at 30/06 vs 3.9bn$ end-2025) after the 500M$ ASR and the Autus bolt-on - the ~5% Omnium EPS haircut vs the prior refresh is entirely carried by named anchors, not a thesis downgrade. Omnium's basis sits structurally ~5% below management-adjusted (recurring litigation partially reintegrated, tax at band top) - a declared, persistent offset.

== THESIS READ ==
- Guidance raised again on revenue (+10-11% cc) with adjusted EPS held 2.95-3.05$: the operational engine outruns the plan while tax absorbs the surplus.
- TMTT +45% cc: the second growth leg is compounding on schedule toward 2bn$/2030.
- The Q4-26 implied EPS (0.53$, below 2025 seasonality) is a TAX phasing effect (Pillar Two/California back-loaded), not operational weakness - verify the actual quarterly tax rate at Q3.
- Net cash rebased by capital returns (ASR) and Autus - finNet drops accordingly in the bridge; not a cash-generation problem (FCF intact).
- Watch: CMS NCD decision (September) and PROGRESS data at TCT - the two catalysts that could re-rate TAVR growth beyond the guide.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: GAAP continuing operations retreated of true one-offs (NOT management-adjusted: recurring litigation only partially excluded, immaterial intangible amortization kept) - the ~5% structural gap to management basis is documented and declared in the scorecard basisNote. Bridge (c-ter): tax 17% (2026) then 19% (top of the guided 16-19% band, Pillar Two + California), interest income on the rebased cash (+47 -> +74M$); the published 2025 reconciles at 14.5% tax and +150M$ interest - explaining the W1 conversion gap (96% -> 83%) by parameters, not error. quarterlyEPS: Q1/Q2 actuals (0.78/0.78), Q3 at guide mid (0.72), Q4 residual (0.53) with the tax-phasing explanation. Scorecard: annual adjusted-EPS guider - anchor 2.975$ (initial Feb guidance, from guidanceHistory), basis offset declared, history to backfill, application suspended. WATCH-LIST: (1) FY26 close: isolate as true one-offs in data the 188.2M$ tax allocation, VIE impairments (163.6M$ YTD), VIE revaluation gains (85.1M$ YTD), HSR penalty (10M$); (2) actual quarterly tax rate at Q3 vs the phasing assumption; (3) TMTT ramp vs 760-780M$; (4) backfill FY24/25 initial guidance anchors. Next useful refresh: Q3 results (late October).

== CATALYSTS ==
CMS NCD decision (Sep 2026); PROGRESS at TCT (H2); PASCAL tricuspid US and next-gen approvals (Q4); TMTT scaling; buyback cadence.
